Marissa / Neha —

From a deal perspective: Greenwave is mid-market with a committed order; they are asking for limits that are not unusual for their vertical. We have leverage on timing and endorsement format but are more constrained on changing published limits unless this is a material expansion of exposure.

Suggested commercial stance:
- Agree to name Greenwave as an additional insured on our GL policy via an endorsement, OR provide an ACORD COI that shows the endorsement reference when available.
- Confirm we will provide a sample COI within 48 hours of countersignature; final COI (with broker) within 5 business days.
- For aggregate limits: offer 1M each occurrence / 2M aggregate for this account for the initial 12 months — but ask legal to keep the MSA base limits and surface this as a committed changes exhibit (order form) rather than editing the master MSA.

I'll support a short alternative we can put in an order form exhibit to avoid changing the core MSA.

Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines (insurance sections) — proposed language

Laura / Tom —

Thanks for the redlines and the clarity on Greenwave's procurement asks. I've reviewed and propose the following approach to keep the MSA stable while meeting Greenwave's commercial needs:

1) Insurance exhibit (order form attachment)
- We will include an Insurance Exhibit in the order form that specifies: 
  "Prior to commencement of Services, Redwood Inference shall procure and maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate, and name Greenwave Technologies as an additional insured with respect to liability arising out of Redwood's performance under this Agreement."

2) Additional insured mechanics
- Rather than editing the MSA blanket section, we'll reference a standard endorsement (ISO CG 20 10 or equivalent) in the exhibit. If Greenwave's broker needs an alternate endorsement form, we can accept the broker's form subject to review.

3) Waiver of subrogation
- We generally accept Waiver of Subrogation to the extent permitted by the insurer; however, we cannot guarantee waiver if the insurer declines. Proposed language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a waiver of subrogation on policies where insurers permit such waiver."

4) COI timing and delivery
- We will deliver a sample COI within 48 hours of countersignature and request the broker to provide a final COI within 5 business days. If Greenwave needs earlier proof (e.g., pre-execution), we can provide a generic sample COI but it will not reference Greenwave by name until ordered.

5) Limits as order-form concession only
- Because changing the base MSA affects all customers, the 1M/2M aggregate concession will be included in the order form exhibit for the term noted above.

I've attached a redlined MSA snippet with the exhibit language inline (see GW_redlines_MSA_20280302_neha.pdf). If this approach works commercially, Marissa — please confirm and we'll prepare the order form exhibit and run the endorsement/COI request with our broker.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
